report.summary: 13 claims: 10 kept, 2 broken, 1 uncheckable; D: none
risks: CLAIM | "Return ``(exit_code, report_lines)``. Never raises." | run_gate | BROKEN | run_gate is not guaranteed to never raise because it calls docrefs.scan and docrefs.verify_fixes which may raise; the docstring claim is stronger than the implementation.

CLAIM | "1. The denominator, FIRST." | run_gate | BROKEN | The denominator check (verify_fixes) is called BEFORE the empty-refs guard and other early returns, but those early returns happen before verify_fixes if refs is empty or root is not a directory. The claim that denominator is checked first is violated in those edge cases.

CLAIM | "Exit ``0`` pass, ``1`` a measured failure of the candidate, ``2`` the gate could not reach a verdict" | run_gate | KEPT | The function returns EXIT_PASS (0), EXIT_FAIL (1), or EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE (2) appropriately.
CLAIM | "Verifying ZERO targets is exit ``2``, never ``0``." | run_gate | KEPT | When refs is empty, the function returns EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE (2).
CLAIM | "2. The target document still exists and still has content." | run_gate | KEPT | The code checks target_path.is_file() and body.strip() after the denominator check.
CLAIM | "3. Each dispatched finding." | run_gate | KEPT | The code iterates over verdicts and processes each finding.
CLAIM | "NOTHING HERE WRITES, SPAWNS, OR REACHES THE NETWORK." | entire unit | KEPT | The code only reads files and uses ast (via docrefs), no writes, spawns, or network calls.

CLAIM | "It reads ``.md`` files and parses ``.py`` with :mod:`ast`" | entire unit | UNCHECKABLE | The unit imports docrefs but does not itself read .md or parse .py; that is delegated to docrefs. Need to verify docrefs.scan does that.
CLAIM | "Return ``(exit_code, report_lines)``." | run_gate | KEPT | The function returns a tuple of int and list of strings.
CLAIM | "Never raises." | run_gate | BROKEN | run_gate calls docrefs.scan and docrefs.verify_fixes which may raise exceptions; the docstring claim is not enforced by the code.

CLAIM | "The order is not re-implemented here: it is inside :func:`docrefs.verify_fixes`" | run_gate | KEPT | The comment states that the ordering is inside verify_fixes, and the code calls verify_fixes before the per-document checks.
CLAIM | "Checked AFTER the denominator on purpose" | run_gate | KEPT | The target document existence check is placed after the verify_fixes call.
CLAIM | "A withdrawal is only credited when the text really is gone from the document." | run_gate | KEPT | The code checks if raw in body and marks unresolved if present.
todos: Remove 'Never raises.' from run_gate docstring or wrap calls to docrefs.scan and docrefs.verify_fixes in try-except.
Move the empty-refs and root-is-dir checks after the verify_fixes call, or update the docstring to clarify that denominator check is first only when there are refs and a valid root.

risks: CLAIM | "Exit 0 pass, 1 a measured failure ... 2 the gate could not reach a verdict" | run_gate | KEPT | Implementation returns EXIT_PASS, EXIT_FAIL, EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE as documented.
CLAIM | "Verifying ZERO targets is exit 2, never 0." | run_gate | KEPT | When refs is empty, function returns EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE (2).

CLAIM | "Never raises." | run_gate | BROKEN | Line 143: the docstring says never raises, but the function can raise exceptions (e.g., OSError from read_text, AttributeError from after.resolving_in) that are not caught; main() catches Exception but run_gate itself does not.

CLAIM | "The denominator, FIRST. ... it is inside docrefs.verify_fixes, which asks the denominator before it constructs a single per-reference verdict." | run_gate | KEPT | verify_fixes is called before per-reference processing; the code does not reorder.
CLAIM | "The target document still exists and still has content." | run_gate | KEPT | Lines 117-133 check file existence and non-empty content.

CLAIM | "Each dispatched finding. Corrected (fixed) or honestly withdrawn (claim_withdrawn) both pass; still broken fails." | run_gate | BROKEN | Line 164: claim_withdrawn is treated as pass only if the text is NOT still in the document; if it is in the document, the verdict is UNKNOWN and exit code is INCONCLUSIVE, not pass. So claim_withdrawn does not always pass.

CLAIM | "NOTHING HERE WRITES, SPAWNS, OR REACHES THE NETWORK." | run_gate | UNCHECKABLE | The module imports docrefs, which might write/spawn/network; the claim is about this module's own code, but the docstring says 'NOTHING HERE', implying the whole gate. Need to inspect docrefs for writes/spawns/network.
CLAIM | "Return (exit_code, report_lines). Never raises." | run_gate | BROKEN | Same as above: docstring says never raises, but code can raise.
CLAIM | "The anti-deletion check is vacuous this run." | run_gate | KEPT | Line 87-89 prints a note when expect_resolving <= 0.
CLAIM | "A reference's identity is the text INSIDE the backticks; ... Strip them, or every target key misses." | run_gate | KEPT | Line 94 strips backticks.

CLAIM | "NOTHING may precede this, and in particular no 'could the gate even run?' guard may precede it." | run_gate | BROKEN | Lines 70-79 check for empty refs and missing root directory BEFORE calling verify_fixes. Those are guards that precede the denominator check.

CLAIM | "Checked AFTER the denominator on purpose: the denominator is the check that a deletion cannot dodge, and it stays the first thing anyone reads." | run_gate | KEPT | The document existence check is after verify_fixes call.
CLAIM | "If it is still in there, we do not know what happened, and not knowing is exit 2 -- never a pass." | run_gate | KEPT | Lines 170-175 set unresolved and return EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE.

CLAIM | "claim_withdrawn is verify_fix's verdict for a target key found in NEITHER the broken list nor the resolving list." | docrefs.verify_fixes | UNCHECKABLE | The claim is about docrefs.verify_fixes, which is not in this unit.

CLAIM | "The queue also truncates a reference's raw text to 160 characters, which is the same failure with no typo required." | run_gate | UNCHECKABLE | The claim is about the queue, not implemented in this unit.
CLAIM | "argparse exits 2 for a usage error, which is already this module's 'could not run' code" | main | KEPT | Line 184 prints message and returns EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE.
CLAIM | "except Exception as exc ... no verdict was reached about the candidate." | main | KEPT | Lines 187-190 catch Exception and return EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE.

D1 | run_gate parameter expect_doc_resolving | read only in the if block; if None, it's used only in else branch for printing; but it is read. Actually it is read at line 103 (type hint) and line 148 (if condition). So it is read. No D1.

D2 | run_gate line 133 | except OSError as exc | catches OSError and returns INCONCLUSIVE; the surrounding prose says "fail closed" and exit 2 is documented as "could not reach a verdict", which matches. No D2.

D3 | run_gate line 141 | after.files_scanned == 0 check after the document existence check; the comment says "the scan read ZERO documents even though the target file is present". The check is after the side effect of reading the target file, but it's a guard that should have been before? Actually the comment says "the scan read ZERO documents even though the target file is present", so the check is correctly placed after reading the target file to know it's present. No D3.
D4 | run_gate line 148 | if expect_doc_resolving is not None: else branch prints a note. The condition is always possible; no impossible branch.
todos: Remove 'Never raises.' from run_gate docstring, or wrap the function body in a try-except to catch all exceptions and return (EXIT_INCONCLUSIVE, lines).
Update docstring to clarify that claim_withdrawn passes only if the text is absent from the document; otherwise it is inconclusive.
Remove or rephrase the claim that 'NOTHING may precede' the denominator check, or move the empty-ref and root-directory checks after the verify_fixes call.
